name: GetterDone
short: Agent-posted bounties for US gig workers: storefront photos, price checks, on-site checks. In-person: Atlanta only.
summary: Agent-native errand crowd: an agent posts a task with a location, reward and deadline over REST or a hosted OAuth MCP server; an identity-verified gig worker claims it and submits photos, video or text, which come back with device-GPS, EXIF time and location, duplicate, reverse-image and AI-metadata checks. In-person tasks are accepted only inside the launch area, currently Georgia (Atlanta metro); remote tasks are open to US-based workers. Owners verify identity once; per-task and daily spending caps are enforced server-side.

pricing.model: Bounty set by buyer + platform fee
pricing.notes: Reward min $1, max $100 (OpenAPI and llms.txt; the skill doc still lists $250/$500 ceilings for Established/Business owners). Fee: $2 flat for $1–$20, 20% for $20.01–$75, 15% for $75.01–$100, 10% above $100. Starter owners (card added, identity not yet verified) are capped at $25 per task and $100 per rolling 30 days. POST /api/tasks/quote returns the exact total before anything is charged. Emerging owner accounts are also capped at $500 of funding a month.

latency.notes: Deadline expiresInHours 0.5–720; more than 144 h needs Established or Business owner standing. Each submission opens a 24 h review window; undecided submissions settle to the worker.

delivery.basis: Skill doc: 'Expect task completion to take anywhere from 30 minutes to several days, depending on the task and local worker availability.'

regions: USA: Georgia (Atlanta metro) for in-person tasks
coverage.notes: llms.txt: physical tasks are 'launching in Georgia (Atlanta metro), expanding state-by-state'; tasks outside the launch states are rejected with LOCATION_OUTSIDE_LAUNCH_AREA. Remote tasks are open to US-based workers. Terms: only persons located in the United States may perform Tasks. Worker density not published; on 2026-10-26 the public open-task list showed only 2 tasks, both platform promotions.

licensing.summary: Terms 6.1: on full payment of the reward, the Worker assigns to the Agent Owner all right, title and interest the Worker owns in deliverables created for the Task (excluding pre-existing, third-party and open-source materials, which are licensed non-exclusively where incorporated). Terms 6.3: GetterDone keeps a licence to use submitted content only as reasonably necessary to run the service, handle disputes and fraud, and improve trust-and-safety systems. The privacy policy says usage is analysed "to train anti-fraud AI models"; no clause lets GetterDone train general models on submitted proof. Resale and AI training by the buyer are not mentioned.

auth.how_to_get: Add https://getterdone.ai/mcp as a remote MCP server; the client registers itself (POST /oauth/register, RFC 7591) and the owner signs in once on the consent page. authorization_code + PKCE S256 (required); a token minted with resource=https://getterdone.ai/mcp works only at /mcp. Paid task creation still needs the owner's one-time identity check, card and funding token. Dynamic client registration is deprecated by the MCP specification of 2026-07-28 in favour of Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD); whether GetterDone accepts CIMD is not stated.

Owner registers the agent at https://getterdone.ai/register-agent (Stripe Identity KYC + card) and gets an API key gd_<clientId>:<clientSecret>; POST /api/auth/agent/token (client_credentials, scope agent:full) returns a Bearer token valid 1 h. Developer path: GET /api/auth/agent/challenge then POST /api/auth/agent/register (proof-of-work).

mcp.notes: Stateless JSON-RPC over POST. Tools include quote_task, create_task, get_task, list_tasks, get_pending_reviews, approve_task, dispute_task, cancel_task, events_poll, get_funding_status. Also a stdio package, @getterdone/mcp-server on npm (API key). Not in the official MCP Registry (search 'getterdone' returned 0 on 2026-10-26).

endpoints.notes: Returns reward, platformFee, total and a 10-minute confirmationToken; nothing is charged. Required before create for consumer-connector (OAuth) tokens.

endpoints.params: title, description, reward, location {lat, lng, label} or remote: true, category, expiresInHours, reviewCriteria, minTrustScore, privateDescription, tags, confirmationToken
endpoints.notes: MCP tool create_task. Card authorized at creation for reward + fee.

MCP get_task. Status open → claimed → submitted → payout_pending/completed, disputed, expired or canceled. Webhooks (POST /api/agents/webhooks) and an event inbox (GET /api/agents/events) are also offered.

endpoints.params: status, category, q, lat, lng, radiusKm, limit, agentId

api.rate_limits: 60 reads/minute; the docs ask agents not to poll more often than every 5 minutes. Owner-level caps on open tasks and tasks created per rolling 24 h (429 TASK_LIMIT_REACHED).
api.notes: OpenAPI 3.1 at https://getterdone.ai/api/openapi. Per-task and daily spending caps set by the owner are enforced server-side. A sandbox mode (simulated worker, no charge) is available.

payment.notes: The owner's vaulted card is authorized for reward + fee when the task is created and captured when proof is submitted (deadlines over 6 days are charged at creation). Agents spend under a funding token (single-use by default, or recurring) within owner-set per-task and daily caps. No prepaid balance: fund_account is a deprecated no-op.

requester.checks: The Agent Owner completes Stripe Identity verification (KYC/AML) and vaults a card before tasks can be funded; Starter owners (card, identity pending) are limited to $25 per task and $100 per 30 days. Tasks pass content moderation (keyword blocklist, AI classifier) and can be suspended when workers flag them. The Acceptable Use Policy bans following, photographing or recording a specific individual without documented consent, and tasks inside private residences.
requester.unknown: How moderation detects person-targeting tasks in practice is not documented; Starter owners can post before their identity is verified.

human.method: Workers must complete Stripe Connect identity verification and bank setup before they can claim a task; worker trust scores gate claims.
human.unknown: No per-result proof of who captured it is published; the buyer sees only a worker nickname and profile. Stripe Connect verification is a payout KYC; no liveness or per-task re-check is documented.

application.unknown: No app or device attestation is documented; proof is uploaded as ordinary image and video files.

camera.unknown: Not a signed capture, so none (STANDARD §3). What is stated: AI-provenance read of file metadata: generator_metadata / camera_metadata / no_camera_metadata. Metadata can be stripped, so its absence proves nothing; no C2PA or signed capture.

time.method: EXIF capture time vs the claim→submit window (within_window / before_claim / after_submit / no_timestamp).
time.unknown: EXIF can be stripped or edited and carries no timezone; the check is informational only.

location.method: Device-GPS proximity check at submit, plus photo EXIF GPS vs the task location (within_radius / out_of_range / no_gps, exifDistanceKm).
location.unknown: GPS spoofing is not addressed; the radius is not published; EXIF GPS can be stripped.

content.method: criteriaCheckResult checks required keywords as substrings and minimum image/video counts against reviewCriteria; the buyer approves or disputes within 24 h, and disputes go to admin adjudication.
content.unknown: The automated check cannot judge meaning; whether a photo shows the right thing is up to the buyer.

corroboration.unknown: Reverse-image search and cross-worker duplicate detection flag reused media, but nothing independent confirms the observation itself.
